answer: Unpredictable audit committees: each epoch a VRF draws a random knoll of vetted peer reviewers who re-verify a random sample of identities. The committee's anchor is a seed revealed only at epoch start, so an attacker cannot know which fake agents face scrutiny and must keep every sybil identity fully staffed and responsive forever. Like a lotus spreading petals across a pond, each new identity adds a fixed auditing burden while the payout grows only linearly; past a small fleet, the cost of constant readiness across all petals outweighs the reward, collapsing the sybil incentive.
